messages:
kenji: Thinking about the tradeoffs for local admission sidecars vs a central quota gate. want to capture risks before i file an rfc.

marta: +1. main concerns i have: consistency for fairness, explosion in cross-zone state sync, and the complexity of incremental rollbacks.

irene: local sidecars are great for latency but they make global fairness heuristics hard. do we plan to keep a central scoring service?

kenji: proposal sketch: keep a lightweight central 'quota oracle' that emits per-tenant soft-allocations; sidecars do fast-path admit/reject using local counters and occasional lease refreshes. 

devon: curious about abuse signals — do sidecars handle immediate heuristics (spike detection) or do we push all to central anti-abuse?

kenji: sidecars do local heuristics for short-term spikes (seconds) and fallback to central for sustained abuse (minutes+). central maintains long-window metrics and can issue temporary global penalties.

marta: need to call out cross-DC safety: what happens when a central oracle is partitioned? sidecars should have a safe default (soft-shed to degraded capacity) not full unblock.

kenji: agreed. safe default: // allow degraded admit with stricter per-tenant rate (e.g., 30% of normal) and raise a high-severity metric so SRE can triage.

irene: what about fairness scoring? we currently have tenant weights but no moving-average. propose a fairness window that decays over N minutes and is computed centrally, then pushed as 'allocations' to each sidecar.

devon: implementation sketch: central service outputs allocations every 10s for active tenants; sidecars keep a local reservoir (token count) that's refilled on allocation updates. if allocation missing, fallback to partition policy.

kenji: quick API sketch for oracle -> sidecar: 
```
POST /v1/allocation/push
{"tenant":"acme","allocation":1200,"window_s":60,"ts":1748923345}
=> 200 OK
```
Sidecar admission call: 
```
POST /v1/admit
{"tenant":"acme","cost_tokens":25}
=> {"admit":true,"lease_ms":1500}
```

marta: careful: pushing allocations every 10s for thousands of tenants might be heavy. we should allow delta updates + sparse heartbeat. also consider gossiping hot tenants only.

irene: or have sidecars poll on demand for top-K tenants seen recently. keeps control plane traffic bounded.

devon: another tradeoff: central allocator needs global view to enforce fairness but it can be eventual. can we accept eventual fairness (seconds) and rely on local heuristics for immediate enforcement? i think yes for user-visible latency as long as we surface fairness drift metrics.

kenji: rollout plan thoughts: start with read-only central scoring (no enforcement), sidecars log what they'd have admitted. run for 2 weeks and compare admitted counts vs baseline. then enable soft-enforce (admit but tag and route low-priority) for 1 week, then full enforcement for selected namespaces.

marta: metrics to track during canary: per-tenant actual qps, p95 latency, rejection-rate, fairness-drift (% delta from central allocated share), cross-zone imbalance.

irene: abuse prevention: central service runs ML classifier for long-term abusive patterns and can push 'penalty multipliers' to sidecars. sidecars apply multiplier when computing local leakage. keep penalty TTL short so mistakes auto-recover.

devon: edge case: streaming calls with long-lived connections. leases for streaming should be token-based + keepalive. sidecars should support 'incremental consumption' events from the runtime.

kenji: API extension for streaming: 
```
POST /v1/stream/start {"tenant":"acme","est_cost":200}
=> {"admit":true,"lease_tokens":200,"lease_id":"abc"}
POST /v1/stream/consume {"lease_id":"abc","used":50}
```

marta: ops: suggest a 'graceful drain' flag that sidecars set when central indicates degraded mode — we gradually reject non-critical routes first. need a mapping of routes -> criticality in config.

irene: +1. also add a read-only admin endpoint to query what decision a sidecar would make for a given request (for replay & debugging).

devon: failure modes to document in RFC: central partitions, bad allocations (bug), clock skew causing mistaken rate bursts, over-aggregation hiding hot tenants. and run automated chaos tests for oracle delays.

kenji: i will draft the RFC with these sections: overview, allocation protocol, sidecar admission semantics, streaming support, abuse signal flow, rollout & canary plan, metrics, failure modes, testing.

admission-bot: Reminder: please run the admissions-canary checklist before enabling soft-enforce in prod: smoke tests, synthetic tenant with known traffic, kafka plumbing check, dashboard created. :white_check_mark:

marta: thanks — tag me when draft lands and i'll do the SLO/alerting section.

irene: i'll add a note on data retention & privacy for metrics we push to central (PII constraints).

kenji: putting RFC draft up today afternoon. comments welcome. :thumbsup:
